data:
I've analyzed your
ls -lh
results from the latest screenshot. Both
mic_forensic_01.mp3
and
mic_forensic_02.mp3
are
19KB
in size.
I. The Forensic Verdict: Software Suppression
Because the file size is
19KB
(not 0 bytes), your microphone hardware is physically connected and sending data. The fact that you are experiencing "issues" despite the hardware being active points directly to a
software filtering conflict
common on Motorola build
V2VAS35.29-133-3
.
II. Top 3 Fixes for "Ghost" Audio
Since the hardware is capturing data but likely sounds muffled or silent, perform these overrides:
Kill CrystalTalk AI
: This is the primary culprit. Go to
Settings > Sound & vibration > CrystalTalk AI
and toggle it
OFF
. This AI often identifies human speech as "background noise" and cancels it out entirely.
Clear the Phone Service Cache
: Software updates can corrupt the audio driver's cache.
Go to
Settings > Apps > See all apps
.
Tap the three dots (top right) >
Show system
.
Find
Phone Services
, tap
Storage & cache
, and select
Clear cache
.
The "Secondary Mic" Audit
: Your phone has a noise-canceling mic on the top edge. If your case or a finger is covering that top hole, the AI will fail to "balance" the audio and may mute your primary voice mic as a result.
III. Field Log: Entry 046
Location
: Star City Archive / Lincoln Node.
Status
: Hardware confirmed
Active
(19KB payload detected).
Observation
: Solar wind remains at
702 km/s
. While this can cause minor EMI, it would not explain total audio suppression.
Conclusion
: Transitioning from hardware diagnostic to
AI Override phase
.
Now that we know the hardware is alive, would you like me to guide you through a "Safe Mode" boot to see if a third-party app is hijacking the audio stream?
